compounds.subtitle: Synthetic heptapeptide · nervous-system research
compounds.category: Human reports exist · clinical benefit unestablished
compounds.summary: Semax is a synthetic peptide studied for possible effects on the nervous system, including research involving ischemic stroke. That interest does not mean a proven treatment has been established.
compounds.unknown: Published studies are not a comprehensive demonstration of safety and effectiveness for broad use. Study quality, replicability, product-specific formulation, and risks remain unresolved.

claims.title: A Semax stroke study was published
claims.text: A 1999 publication describes an investigation involving people during acute ischemic stroke. A published study is not enough, by itself, to establish an effective treatment.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: One human publication is a starting point for evaluating methods, outcomes, and replication, not a treatment endorsement.

claims.title: FDA identifies compounding safety questions
claims.text: FDA reports potential immunogenicity and peptide-related impurity concerns for compounded Semax, with limited safety information for proposed routes.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: An FDA safety-risk assessment is a warning about unresolved risks, not an FDA-approved indication.

claims.title: Marketing claims require separate verification
claims.text: A supplier certificate can report chemical analyses for a sample, but does not establish the effectiveness of Semax in people or whether the tested lot was what customers received.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Chemical composition, human benefit, and product-lot identity need different evidence.

plainEnglish.simple: Semax is a man-made peptide being studied for how it might affect the brain and nerves. It is not an FDA-approved treatment in the United States.
plainEnglish.interest: Researchers have explored whether it affects brain responses after a stroke. Online sellers also advertise it for focus and memory, but those claims need separate proof.
plainEnglish.human: Older, limited human research exists, including a Russian-language stroke investigation. That is not enough to conclude Semax improves stroke recovery, focus or memory for most people.
plainEnglish.caution: We still need stronger, independent human trials and better information about long-term safety. FDA has also highlighted possible risks when Semax is used in compounded preparations.

compounds.name: GHK-Cu
compounds.subtitle: Copper-binding tripeptide complex · tissue/skin research
compounds.summary: GHK-Cu is a copper-associated form of the tripeptide GHK. Researchers have explored tissue remodeling and skin-related effects, but different chemical formulations and delivery routes matter.
compounds.unknown: Human evidence is limited and formulation-dependent. Much of the supporting work is laboratory or animal research; injectable safety and therapeutic efficacy are not established.

claims.title: Rat wound experiments found matrix changes
claims.text: An experimental rat model reported increased collagen and related extracellular-matrix measures following GHK-Cu exposure.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: A biological effect in rat tissue is not proof of faster or safer wound healing in people.

claims.title: A 2026 review highlights formulation gaps
claims.text: A scientific review found sparse clinical evidence and emphasized differences in copper binding, chemical species, delivery, and measurement methods.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Two products labeled GHK-Cu may not be analytically equivalent merely because the label uses the same name.

claims.title: Injectable GHK-Cu has FDA-identified concerns
claims.text: FDA identifies possible immune reactions and peptide-related impurities for compounded GHK-Cu delivered by injectable routes.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: These route-specific concerns cannot be resolved by a single purity percentage on a certificate.

plainEnglish.simple: GHK-Cu is a short peptide bound to copper. It is studied for its role in skin and tissue repair.
plainEnglish.interest: It appears in skincare marketing because laboratory and animal studies suggest it can affect processes involved in building and repairing tissue.
plainEnglish.human: Small cosmetic studies exist, with mixed findings. Most detailed evidence comes from lab or animal work. That is different from showing an injectable product improves healing in people.
plainEnglish.caution: The formulation and whether it goes on the skin or is injected make a major difference. FDA has flagged potential safety concerns for injectable compounded GHK-Cu.

compounds.name: TB-500
compounds.subtitle: Marketed peptide name · thymosin beta-4 fragment identity varies
compounds.category: Preclinical fragment research · human benefit unproven
compounds.summary: TB-500 is a research-marketing name often associated with a short thymosin beta-4-derived fragment. Full-length thymosin beta-4 and individual fragments are chemically different and should never share evidence automatically.
compounds.unknown: A seller must document the exact molecular identity and lot. Most cited repair data come from animal experiments, and FDA identifies important human safety-data gaps for the fragment.

claims.title: An identified TB-500 preparation contained a fragment
claims.text: An analytical paper identified the N-terminally acetylated thymosin beta-4 fragment Ac-LKKTETQ in material described as TB-500.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: The phrase TB-500 alone does not guarantee a particular formulation; inspect the exact sequence and report.

claims.title: Thymosin beta-4 and fragment studied in wound models
claims.text: Researchers observed wound-repair changes in rat and mouse models with thymosin beta-4 and an active fragment. These are not human clinical treatment outcomes.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Results for full-length thymosin beta-4 do not automatically transfer to a product advertised as TB-500.

claims.title: FDA reports inadequate human exposure evidence
claims.text: FDA identifies immunogenicity and impurity concerns for compounded thymosin beta-4 fragment (LKKTETQ), also referred to as TB-500.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Absence of identified human exposure data means the safety uncertainty should remain visible.

plainEnglish.simple: TB-500 is a name used in peptide marketing. A laboratory paper identified a short piece of a larger protein called thymosin beta-4 in one TB-500 sample.
plainEnglish.interest: People talk about it in relation to injury and tissue repair because animal studies have investigated thymosin beta-4 and related pieces.
plainEnglish.human: The cited repair results were mainly seen in animals, not established treatments for human injuries. Studies of full-length thymosin beta-4 cannot automatically be applied to every TB-500 product.
plainEnglish.caution: The exact chemical identity may differ across listings, and we lack good evidence of safety and effectiveness for marketed TB-500 in people.

compounds.subtitle: Small-molecule NNMT inhibitor · not a peptide

compounds.summary: 5-Amino-1MQ (5A1MQ) is a small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). It belongs in the adjacent-compounds directory, not the peptide category.
compounds.unknown: The cited weight and metabolic findings come from diet-induced obese mice. This limited desk review found no basis to claim clinical effectiveness or an established safe human treatment.

claims.text: Primary pharmacology research describes 5A1MQ as a small-molecule NNMT inhibitor. It is not a peptide.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Not everything listed on a peptide-selling website is actually a peptide.

claims.title: Mouse studies reported metabolic effects
claims.text: A published animal study found changes in weight, fat mass, glucose-related measures, and liver markers in mice after NNMT-inhibitor treatment.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Mouse results cannot be treated as proof of human weight loss or medical safety.

claims.title: Related mouse research supports studying the enzyme
claims.text: An earlier paper tested other small-molecule inhibitors of the same NNMT enzyme in cells and mice. It did not show that 5-Amino-1MQ works in humans.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: Multiple animal studies may strengthen a research idea, but still cannot prove a treatment works in people.

plainEnglish.simple: 5-Amino-1MQ is not a peptide. It is a small molecule studied for blocking an enzyme called NNMT, which is involved in how cells process certain substances.
plainEnglish.interest: Researchers are exploring whether blocking NNMT changes how the body handles fat and energy.
plainEnglish.human: Studies cited here found effects in mice. That tells researchers what might be worth studying next, not that the substance causes safe weight loss in people.
plainEnglish.caution: Useful human trials and long-term safety evidence are missing from this review. A mouse result should never be presented as a proven human benefit.

plainEnglish.simple: CJC-1295 is a man-made peptide designed to encourage the body to release growth hormone.

plainEnglish.caution: FDA reports safety concerns, including faster heart rate and other reactions. Also, products labeled “CJC-1295 with DAC” and “without DAC” should not be assumed identical.

claims.meaning: A positive phase 3 trial is substantial human evidence, but it does not by itself mean a marketed drug has FDA approval.

claims.title: A second large 2026 trial included people with type 2 diabetes

claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending

claims.title: FDA warns against unapproved retatrutide sales and compounding
claims.text: FDA states that retatrutide has not been found safe and effective for a marketed indication, cannot be used in federal compounding pathways, and warns about research-labeled products sold for human use.
claims.review: Source-linked desk draft · qualified reviewer pending
claims.meaning: A supplier website advertising retatrutide is not a licensed prescription-drug supply channel.

plainEnglish.simple: Retatrutide is an experimental medicine that acts on three hormone-receptor systems involved in blood sugar, appetite and metabolism. It is not FDA-approved as of this research date.
plainEnglish.interest: Researchers are testing whether it can help people with obesity and related conditions.
plainEnglish.human: Large randomized trials published in 2026 reported substantial average weight changes in the people studied. Common side effects involved the stomach and digestive system. Results are promising but do not make it an approved medicine.
plainEnglish.caution: Further safety monitoring and regulatory review matter. Products advertised for sale as “research retatrutide” are not shown to match the medicine used in clinical trials.
